title: SSE bitmap/chunk loss debug scratch
content:
Goal: capture a minimal, repeatable repro and a short theory for the intermittent chunk-loss / partial-frame hang seen in prod streaming traces. This is a scratchpad — rough timeline, commands I ran, log excerpts, and experiment ideas.

Summary of symptom
- Client receives SSE stream but sometimes sees missing "data:" events (partial frames) or a final truncated chunk. Happens ~1-2% of streams for certain model sizes (long-context > 4k tokens) under moderate concurrency.
- Failure class: chunk boundary corruption (boundary present but payload stops mid-json) or a gap where a whole event is not delivered. Often followed by client reconnect and immediate continuation (server-side resumed using KV cache) — suggests server queued tokens but TCP/connection-level issue dropped bytes.

Timeline + quick notes
- 2026-02-10: First saw on staging with load test (k6) hitting dedicated pool (p4d). Repro rate ~0.7%.
- 2026-02-12: Added logging in streaming runtime for chunk send sizes and last-kv-seq. No clear pattern; affected streams show normal send sizes until the truncated frame.
- 2026-02-15: Hypothesis: continuous batching + partial write via sendmsg with iovec may interleave with eviction path leading to a stale buffer referenced after free. No OOMs observed.
- 2026-02-18: Started manual reproducer from laptop (below). Added tcpdump around request time. Observed a FIN shortly after truncated chunk in some traces.

Exact commands I used (repro attempts)
1) curl SSE simple (baseline)
- curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-13b" > /tmp/stream.out
- Notes: this mostly works; low signal because curl reconnects silently.

2) netcat style read to force visible truncation
- printf 'GET /v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-13b HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.dev\r\nAccept: text/event-stream\r\nAuthorization: Bearer $TOKEN\r\nConnection: keep-alive\r\n\r\n' | nc api.redwood.dev 443 > raw.out
- Observed TLS layer complicates capture; switched to port-forward to staging pod.

3) pod-forward and curl (staging)
- kubectl port-forward svc/streaming-staging 8080:8080 -n serving-runtime &
- curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-13b" > pf.out
- Then: tcpdump -i lo -w pf.pcap & (while reproducing)
- Filter pcap for RST/FIN around the event timestamp. Found FIN in ~40% of repro runs where truncation happened.

4) python client that prints raw bytes and framing
- python3 - <<PY
import requests, sys
r = requests.get('http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-13b', headers={"Accept":"text/event-stream","Authorization":f"Bearer {os.environ['TOKEN']}"}, stream=True)
buf = b''
for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=64):
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"--- CHUNK ---\n")
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(chunk)
    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
PY
- Found cases where chunk boundaries align with mid-JSON and then next chunk never arrives (connection closed).

Representative truncated output (copied from pf.out)
-----BEGIN TRUNCATED EVENT-----
data: {"id":"evt_1567","delta":" partially generated text here, "}
data: {"id":"evt_1568","delta":"more text","finish_reason":"stop"}
data: {"id":"evt_1569","delta":"incomplete JSON start {\"text\": \"This is a long sentence that\"\n--EOF (connection closed)
-----END-----

Runtime logs around send (from streaming agent)
[2026-02-15 14:32:06.421][info][stream] send_chunk: stream_id=abc123 size=192 iov=2
[2026-02-15 14:32:06.422][debug][iov] iov0.len=128 iov1.len=64 ptr=0x7f9b000
[2026-02-15 14:32:06.423][info][kvcache] last_seq_sent=2741
[2026-02-15 14:32:06.426][warn][net] write returned EPIPE for stream=abc123
[2026-02-15 14:32:06.427][info][stream] conn_closed_by_peer stream_id=abc123 bytes_sent=576

Observations from logs
- EPIPE / write error shows up right after send_chunk in many failed traces. Means peer closed read side. But why would client close mid-stream? Some clients do aggressive timeouts under high mem pressure.
- In some successful traces we also see FIN but full event delivered — maybe FIN race during idle keep-alive after chunk.

Theories (ranked)
1) Client-level timeouts/reconnects: certain SDKs (older node-fetch) close socket when internal buffer threshold reached. But we reproduced with python requests with stream=True too — less likely to be all clients.
2) In-kernel send buffer drop under heavy load where kernel reports partial write and we don't handle it correctly (we assume write completed). Check code path that treats sendmsg return value and iov offsets.
3) Post-send buffer reuse/free race: runtime reuses buffer backing iovec before async TLS write completes -> garbage bytes or missing subsequent writes. Memory sanitizer didn't catch because only happens under concurrency.
4) Proxy/loadbalancer (envoy) in path closing connection due to perceived idle or header size issues when continuous streaming with intermittent pauses. Packet captures show FIN from server side IP in several cases which is suspicious.

Experiments to run next
- Instrument write path to log sendmsg return values and iov offsets (exactly how many bytes written). Add telemetry metric: partial-write-count per stream.
- Add optional delay to reuse of buffers (sleep 5ms after queueing to TLS write) to see if race goes away in staging. Quick toggle via env flag.
- Reproduce with plain HTTP (no TLS) in local cluster to eliminate OpenSSL async layer. Already did kubectl port-forward -> that still uses local TLS termination? Ensure we hit the pod directly and not an ingress.
- Run targeted load test with different client libraries (node fetch, node native http, python requests, curl) to see client-specific rates.
- Force keep-alive vs Connection: close to observe different behavior.
- Deploy a patch: handle partial write properly by looping over iovec until all bytes written or transient EAGAIN/EINTR, and only free buffers after confirmed bytes_sent == total_len. Roll out to a small subset (canary).

Small diagnostic patches I tried (notes)
- Patch A (added logging of sendmsg returns): increased visibility; found some sendmsg return values = 0 during that time => kernel not accepting data (backpressure).
- Patch B (delay reuse): locally reduced repro from 0.7% -> 0.05% in short runs; suggests race.
- Patch C (looping write till consumed): needs more testing on perf. Might add CPU overhead but correctness first.

Immediate action items
- Create PR with additional send-return handling and telemetry. Reference: GH PR 4821 (linked above).
- Add eBPF probe on staging to count retransmits and socket reset cause codes for affected pod.
- Prep a canary rollout with Patch C for 5% of traffic and monitor truncated_event_rate metric (new telemetry).

Open questions / unknowns
- Why do some FINs originate from server IP vs client IP? Need to correlate with envoy logs (ingress vs pod).
- Are there kernel-level limits being hit during quantization/large-context runs (e.g., backlog size)? Check net.core.wmem default values and adjust in staging as experiment.
- Is the TLS lib performing async flush in a way that can race with our buffer reuse? Need to instrument OpenSSL callbacks.

Quick checklist for next run (on staging)
- [ ] Enable send-return telemetry on streaming pod image (build w/ flag)
- [ ] Start tcpdump with ring buffer (rotate) around test window
- [ ] Run k6 scenario: 200 concurrents, 10s think, model=redwood-13b, 10k requests
- [ ] Collect pf.pcap + runtime logs + envoy logs + kernel drop counters

Notes for whoever picks this up
- Start with Patch B (delay reuse) locally — fastest to test. If repro goes away, it strongly points to reuse race.
- Perf regression expected for Patch C (looping writes) but should be negligible compared to long-model compute time; still bench.
- Link to similar past incident: INF-1180 (SSE partial frames 2025) — might reuse some instrumentation there.

Raw saved artifacts
- pf.pcap (staging run 2026-02-18) saved to /tmp/pf-20260218.pcap
- runtime logs: /var/log/serving/stream-agent/stream-2026-02-15.log
- small repro script: scripts/local_sse_repro.py (WIP)

End of scratchpad.
